### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **22** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx`  _(via autoRestart (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_HEALTH_CHECK_KEYS))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via watchPatterns (literal, a string literal in RETIRED_HOT_RELOAD_KEYS))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **141** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2a30eb07af4f181d59ddf815317634be2b608708` — the merge of head `68ff8a108271c6c4ce40db16bf5e80a171046ea5` into base `eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2a30eb07af4f181d59ddf815317634be2b608708 && git checkout 2a30eb07af4f181d59ddf815317634be2b608708
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8 68ff8a108271c6c4ce40db16bf5e80a171046ea5 && git checkout -B drift-repro eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8 && git merge --no-ff 68ff8a108271c6c4ce40db16bf5e80a171046ea5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eff0a9622340f59068651f2b82d4afcd177546a8` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Seat note — the one red is the SEAT's defect, not this PR's, and the drift advisory is clear, 2026-09-22T04:40Z

`domain:spec` seat 4, the seat that dispatched #18048. ⛔ No code change is asked for by this comment.

### 🔴 «The card this PR closes must claim this branch» — mine, already repaired card-side

`scripts/check-closing-target-claim.mjs` requires the closed card's NEWEST `Claim:` comment to carry a parseable `Branch:` line naming this PR's head (`:606`; the refusal text at `:770` is «its newest `Claim:` comment carries no parseable `Branch:` line»). My claim on #18048 carried none: I wrote it before the dev existed, so there was no branch to name, and I left the line out rather than predicting one. The gate is right about the order — a branch is `claude/issue-<N>-<slug>` by construction and the claim could have prescribed it.

⇒ repaired by an amended claim on #18048 naming `claude/issue-18048-spec-18-tombstone-gate`. ⚠️ **A card comment does not re-fire this check** — `closing-target-claim-guard.yml` is `pull_request`-triggered, so it re-runs on this PR's next push. If the head does not move again, the seat spends its one budgeted re-run on it; ⛔ never an empty commit and ⛔ never a close-and-reopen.

Process change so this does not recur: the branch name now goes into the dispatch word, so the claim carries `Branch:` in the same act. The same amendment was written pre-emptively on #14512 before its PR opened.

### 📓 Docs Drift Check — measured, and nothing is owed

The advisory names two pages. Both answered here so nobody re-derives them:

- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/lifecycle.mdx` (hand-written, via `autoRestart`) — **already in this diff** (+1 −1). Covered.
- ⛔ `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx` (RELEASE-OWNED, read-only, via `watchPatterns`) — **it does not carry this card's subject at all.** `@objectstack/spec 18` and the backticked `` `@objectstack/spec` 18 `` both return **0 files** across `content/docs/releases`, measured with two lit controls so the zero is a reading rather than a dark instrument: `watchPatterns` returns 1 hit in that exact file, and `@objectstack/spec` returns 10 files across that tree. ⇒ ⛔ nothing to fix there, and ⛔ nobody should edit it — AGENTS.md's Documentation Guardrails make a code PR editing `content/docs/releases/` the exact thing that guardrail exists to stop.

⚠️ One thing the advisory says about itself that is worth carrying rather than skimming: `packages/core/PHASE2_IMPLEMENTATION.md` yielded **no anchor**, so pages documenting it are NOT COVERED by that run. That is an unread surface, ⛔ not a clean bill of health — and this PR does change that file (+2 −2).

### On the new gate, for whoever reviews it

The three sites that must stay UNTOUCHED are not in this diff, which is correct: `docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md` (the ruling quoting the defect), `docs/v17-docs-sweep.md` (the detection fingerprint for this very class) and `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.test.ts` (a synthetic fixture that must name a version which does not exist). ⭐ The gate's hardest requirement is that it can tell a tombstone from a quotation of a bad tombstone — a gate that cannot will red on the ruling that forbids the bug.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `68ff8a108271c6c4ce40db16bf5e80a171046ea5`

At-tier review, spawned because the `domain:spec` seat's own served tier is unmeasured and may
not self-review. Everything below is measured at this head on a tree verified byte-identical to
it; the dev's report and the seat's claim comment were treated as claims to test, not as input.
Reviewed 2026-09-22T05:05Z; the C6 row quoted is the reading taken 2026-09-22T04:45Z.

### ① Derived judgments

**`Clause-②: no` is correct.** Re-measured independently, not adopted.

The mechanism settles it. `retiredKey(guidance)` in `packages/spec/src/shared/retired-key.ts` is
a `z.never()` carrying an error thunk that returns `guidance`, then `.optional()`, then
`.describe('[REMOVED] ' + guidance)` — accept/reject is fixed entirely by the combinator (only absence is accepted, any authored value refused), and
`guidance` participates solely as the refusal message and the description. No string in this diff
can move an accept/reject result for any input, because no string in this diff is read to decide
one.

The diff agrees. All 37 replaced lines sit inside string literals, JSDoc comments or Markdown:
filtering the `packages/spec` diff for `export`, a `z.` combinator, `.optional()` or `retiredKey(`
returns nothing at all. No declaration, no type, no key list, no enum member moves.

On the PM's control I measured something stronger than its "0 hits". `packages/spec/api-surface`
and `packages/spec/export-origins` are the only two such directories in the tree, and they carry
exported symbol names and their origins only — `was removed in @objectstack/spec` occurs 0 times
across both, and the single `@objectstack/spec` hit per file is the artifact's own `description`
header. These baselines cannot carry a tombstone sentence by construction, so the ground for `no`
is structural rather than a count that a later edit could move. Two further controls: no committed
JSON artifact carries these sentences, and no non-test code string-matches the messages.

The regeneration claim holds. `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated` reports
`check:docs content/docs/references/**` green, so the 7 rows under
`content/docs/references/kernel/` are byte-exact `gen:docs` output projected from the moved zod
docblocks, never hand-edited. That aggregate exits 1 here on one artifact only, `api-surface`, and
its own output states the reason: it measured against a `packages/spec/dist` found on disk and not
built by that run. Since the diff changes no exported symbol, a name-and-origin baseline cannot
move; this is a stale local `dist`, not a finding against the PR.

Counts verified against the diff rather than the report: 22 in-class sites now name `17.3.0` and
14 name the bare published major `17`, plus the one declared bounded-in-place fix, for 37 replaced
lines across fifteen files. The split reconciles exactly. The three quotation sites the dev says
are untouched — ADR-0087, `docs/v17-docs-sweep.md`, `retired-key.test.ts` — are absent from the
changed-file list, confirmed.

### ② Semver level

**`patch` for both `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/core` is the right level.** What moved is
refusal-message text, docblock prose and doc pages. No declaration and no accept/reject behaviour
changes, so there is nothing for `minor` or `major` to carry.

The interaction named in the dispatch needs one correction, because as stated it predicts a red
that does not and should not occur. The carrier axis in `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`
reaches its `enforce` verdict (exit 1) only when the clause-② axis is **CARRIED** *and* every moved
package is graded `patch` with none at `minor` or above. "Carried" means `Clause-②: yes`, or `no`
bearing a `narrowing` arm. This PR declares `no` with no arm, so the verdict is `not-declared`,
which exits 0 before the grading branch is reachable. All-`patch` alone never reds it. Measured:
`Check Changeset` is `success` on this head.

Worth recording that this makes ① load-bearing for ②. Had `Clause-②` been `yes`, two packages both
graded `patch` with none at `minor` or above is exactly the `enforce` shape, and `Check Changeset`
would have gone red. The green is conditional on the declaration being right, which is why it was
re-measured here rather than adopted.

### ③ Boundary flags

The gate closes the class it was built for. Production pass exits 0 with 39 live sites across 17
files reduced to 0; `--self-test` passes 29 of 29; `check:self-test-wired` exits 0 over 223
scripts, so the self-test is genuinely run by CI through the pnpm script. Two axes I probed rather
than took on trust: a citation inside a three-backtick fence in a tracked `.md` reds correctly (the
fence axis is genuinely closed), and a new live tombstone in a newly tracked `.ts` file reds
correctly (the corpus is the tracked file set, so PR-added files are scanned). Four residuals
follow. None blocks landing — each is fail-closed or needs a deliberate, reviewable edit — but the
first materially qualifies a claim in the PR body.

**B1 — R2's `witness` has no minimum specificity, so one later edit degrades the ledger from a
sentence claim into a count-pinned file allowlist.** Measured: setting an entry's witness to `/./`
and leaving `covers` untouched stays green, proving nothing requires the regex to describe
anything; then swapping one covered sentence for an entirely different sentence at the same major,
keeping the count, *also* stays green. The advertised self-invalidation — "editing the quotation
away kills its exemption instead of leaving a hole" — holds only while the witness is specific, and
nothing enforces that. The `covers` pin does survive: a genuinely *new* citation still moves the
count and reds, so this is not an unbounded path allowlist and the PR body's claim stands in its
count limb. It does not stand in its witness limb. A minimum-specificity assertion on `witness`, or
a battery that swaps a covered sentence under a broadened witness, would close it.

**B2 — a latent triple false-red on the day `@objectstack/spec` reaches major 18.** Measured by
bumping the local manifest to `18.0.0`: the gate exits 1 with three problems, none of them a real
defect. `SELF_FIXTURE_FLOOR` counts citations *above* the published major, so the script's own
18-fixtures stop counting and it reads 10 against a floor of 12 — and the remedy text says "Restore
the fixtures" for fixtures nobody removed. The two major-18 ledger entries then red as "matched
NOTHING ... The quotation moved or was edited away", because a citation at or below the published
major is skipped before the ledger is consulted; the quotations did not move, the class moved past
them. The self-test battery labelled "the class is DERIVED — the same corpus is green once the tree
reaches 18" passes only because it supplies an empty ledger and no self-path, so it does not cover
the real configuration and the label overstates what it tests. Fail-closed and loud, at a
high-ceremony event whose remedy is deleting two obsolete entries and re-pinning the floor, so this
is maintenance debt rather than a hole — but it should be written down now, while the reason is
known, instead of being rediscovered as a mystery red during a major bump.

**B3 — R1 is applied by file text, not by file type.** Measured with a tracked `.ts` probe: the
plain tombstone reds, and the identical sentence wrapped in a double-backtick span goes green. In
TypeScript double backticks carry no Markdown meaning and would sit literally in the operator-facing
refusal string, so the abuse is visible in review and produces a malformed message — but it is a
bypass that needs no ledger entry, no witness and no count pin. Scoping R1 to Markdown-family
extensions is a one-line tightening and would make the rule mean what the PR body says it means.

**B4 — the self-exclusion floor is a tripwire, not a ratchet.** The script carries 28 citations
above the published major against a floor of 12, so up to 16 of the adversarial fixtures, well over
half, can be deleted silently. It does catch wholesale gutting, which is what the compensating
control is for; the report's "gutting its fixtures reds the gate on itself" is true only below 12.
A shrink-only pin at the measured 28 would match the ratchet convention used elsewhere in this
tree.

**B5, noted not charged** — the class can red a legitimate forward-looking citation, and the only
escape is a ledger entry whose `kind` vocabulary is `quotation` or `measurement`, neither of which
honestly describes a genuine plan. Acceptable today, because ADR-0087 makes dating a retirement to
the next major wrong by ruling.

**One measured contradiction of the dev's report.** The PR body's census table gives the dotted
`17.x` control after the change as 511 sites / 113 files. The gate's own `--census` at this head
reads **512 / 113**. A one-site understatement in a control reading, not in the finding set, which
is 0 either way — but the body presents that table as re-runnable at this head, and it does not
reproduce exactly.

**CI is converged and clean.** Judged on what I measured from the API, not on the report. All 36
check-runs on this head are terminal — 34 `success`, 2 `skipped`, none failing, none pending — and
`Lint & Repo Gates`, the job that carries the new gate, is green. This record was deliberately held
until that job landed: a PASS on a head whose CI never finished is worthless.

The one red flagged in dispatch as the seat's, «The card this PR closes must claim this branch»,
had fired against a state that predates the card-side repair — it completed roughly nine minutes
*before* the card's governing claim naming `claude/issue-18048-spec-18-tombstone-gate` was posted.
It has since re-run and now passes, which is the reading I judged it on rather than the
explanation. No red is outstanding, seat's or this PR's.
